data:
Status: planned (wave 3). There is no repository and no code yet, and fem is a working name. These pages describe the plan, not a release.
Lagrange finite elements, quadrature, assembly, boundary conditions and the first PDE solvers.
data.depends-on#Depends on: go-geometry for meshes, and go-sparse for the linear solvers (its iterative solvers are released; direct solvers are planned for wave 3).
data.how-it-will-be-validated#How it will be: Method of manufactured solutions: observed convergence order within 0.1 of theory, h^(p+1) in L2 and h^p in H1 for Pp elements. Relative L2 error against the exact solution and the relative residual of the linear solve. A solution is never compared with an oracle’s mesh node by node; the oracle runs on the same mesh.
data.reference-implementations-and-licences#R:
What exists, under which licence, and what that allows:
Implementation Licence and use MFEM BSD-3-Clause; a clean design reference for elements and assembly deal.II Apache-2.0 with LLVM exception on one side, LGPL-2.1+ on the other: the Apache side may be ported after checking each file’s SPDX header FEniCS / DOLFINx LGPL-3.0: an oracle only, on a Linux lane GPL, LGPL, AGPL and non-free code is never ported: it is only run as an oracle, as an external program.
data.references#References:
The algorithms and the theory the package will start from, as the roadmap’s bibliography lists them:
Reference Cite Brenner, Scott, The Mathematical Theory of Finite Element Methods, Springer doi:10.1007/978-0-387-75934-0 Ern, Guermond, Theory and Practice of Finite Elements, Springer, 2004 doi:10.1007/978-1-4757-4355-5 Logg, Mardal, Wells (eds.), Automated Solution of Differential Equations by the Finite Element Method, Springer, 2012 doi:10.1007/978-3-642-23099-8 Dunavant, High degree efficient symmetrical Gaussian quadrature rules for the triangle, IJNME 21(6):1129-1148, 1985 doi:10.1002/nme.1620210612 Xiao, Gimbutas, A numerical algorithm for the construction of efficient quadrature rules in two and higher dimensions, Comput. Math. Appl. 59(2):663-676, 2010 doi:10.1016/j.camwa.2009.10.027 LeVeque, Finite Volume Methods for Hyperbolic Problems, CUP, 2002 (for the finite-volume work the plan lists at lower priority) doi:10.1017/CBO9780511791253
data.scope-notes#Scope notes: The plan treats this as an extra-large item, and the MATLAB PDE Toolbox surface is far larger than the Poisson-first plan covers. 3D meshing, Stokes and general elasticity are multi-year.
data.what-it-will-provide#What it will provid: elements Lagrange P1 and P2 on triangles quadrature tabulated symmetric Gauss rules on the triangle assembly stiffness and mass matrices assembled into go-sparse containers, with Dirichlet, Neumann and periodic boundary conditions equations Poisson first, then heat, wave and elasticity; Stokes later
data.where-the-plan-lives#Where the plan live: PLAN.md, STATUS.md and the bibliography in the go-scikit roadmap.

Status: planned (wave 3). There is no repository and no code yet, and mms is a working name. These pages describe the plan, not a release.
The shared method-of-manufactured-solutions convergence harness.
data.depends-on#Depends on: nothing; it is small and independent, and is listed first in the plan’s priorities.
data.how-it-will-be-validated#How it will be: The harness is itself tested on a problem whose convergence order is known, so that a wrong order is reported as wrong.
data.reference-implementations-and-licences#R:
What exists, under which licence, and what that allows:
Implementation Licence and use no external corpus the method needs none: the exact solution is chosen GPL, LGPL, AGPL and non-free code is never ported: it is only run as an oracle, as an external program.
data.references#References:
The algorithms and the theory the package will start from, as the roadmap’s bibliography lists them:
Reference Cite Brenner, Scott, The Mathematical Theory of Finite Element Methods, Springer (the a priori error estimates it checks) doi:10.1007/978-0-387-75934-0
data.scope-notes#Scope notes: Two further items sit at the lowest priority in the plan and are not scheduled: a one-dimensional method of lines (a pdepe analogue over go-numerics/integrate) and finite differences and volumes on structured grids.
data.what-it-will-provide#What it will provid: harness pick an exact solution, derive the source term and boundary data, run a refinement sequence, and report the observed convergence order use the test kit of the other packages of the organization, and of anyone validating a PDE solver
